tldr: The identified lower bound \(B(P)\) measures residual treatment-effect variation within covariate strata. Its first derivative vanishes at conditional equality, while its quadratic derivative retains the diagonal of the continuous covariate distribution. The research question determines matching localized absolute-risk and globally honest connected-interval length frontiers on a fixed randomized three-covariate sectional-smoothness class, including every shrinking radius and the full equality null. A positive-density pilot, covariate projection, and centered transport correction provide a concrete starting handle; the rates, logarithms, and cost of one radius-blind interval are outputs. The contribution is the uniform nonlinear statistical and numerical certificate with matching original-record converses. Identification, quadratic-functional projection principles, regular transport inference, and equality collapse are inherited. The intended consumer is a residual-variance extension of dualbounds, with mean subtraction inside each covariate stratum.
gap: Lin--Gao--Blanchet--Glynn identify conditional transport bounds and establish generic plug-in rates; their smooth-density follow-up already supplies quadratic stability and records equality variance collapse. Its regular inference theorem requires joint smoothness that the fixed sectional class need not possess. Ji--Lei--Spector supply conservative dual-bound inference, including a qualified shrinking-variance extension. None of these checked results matches both all-radius absolute risk and globally honest local expected length for \(B\) on the specified original-record class.
